sections.h2: Where is Waltham, and which offices handle its property tax?
sections.html:
Waltham is a city in Middlesex County, Massachusetts, about 9 miles west of Downtown Boston, and two separate City Hall offices handle its property tax. The Assessors set the value of each parcel, and the Treasurer/Collector sends the bills and takes the payments.

The city covers 13.76 square miles, of which 12.75 is land. It shares borders with Watertown and Belmont to the east, Lexington to the north, Lincoln and Weston to the west and Newton to the south. Waltham is run by a mayor and a city council, and it was incorporated as a city in 1884.

OfficeWhat it doesWhere and how to reach it
Assessors OfficeValues property, handles abatements, exemptions and the tax relief programCity Hall, 25 Lexington Street, 781-314-3200
Treasurer/CollectorIssues and collects real estate bills, handles tax title and municipal lien certificates610 Main Street, 781-314-3250, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

If a question is about the amount of the bill, call the Assessors. If it is about where to send a payment or how much is owed today, call the Collector.

sections.h2: When are Waltham real estate tax bills due?
sections.html:
Waltham bills real estate tax four times a year, with payments due on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. The city's fiscal year starts on July 1, and if a due date lands on a weekend the bill is due the next business day.

QuarterDue dateType of bill
FirstAugust 1Preliminary, based on last year's tax
SecondNovember 1Preliminary, based on last year's tax
ThirdFebruary 1Actual, based on this year's assessment and rate
FourthMay 1Actual, based on this year's assessment and rate

The Treasurer/Collector counts a payment as made when the office receives it. The city also says that if no bill arrives 30 days before a due date, you should call the office for a copy. Unpaid bills carry interest at 14 percent a year, according to the Collector's real estate page.

sections.h2: Why are the third and fourth quarter bills in Waltham usually higher?
sections.html:
The last two bills are higher because the first two are only estimates. The Assessors explain that the first and second quarter bills add up to about half of the prior year's taxes, and they ignore your new assessment and the new tax rate.

The third and fourth quarter bills then true up the year. The city adds up your full actual tax, subtracts what you paid in the first two quarters, and splits the remainder in two. Any rise in value, any change in the rate and any betterment charge all land in those last two bills.

Three situations make the jump bigger than owners expect:

  • Your assessment rose faster than the city's overall levy.
  • Betterments, special assessments or interest were added during the year.
  • The home was sold and the previous owner had a personal exemption that does not pass to the buyer.

For a seller, this timing matters at closing, because a bill paid in August can still be followed by a larger balance in February.

sections.h2: Who is named on the bill when a Waltham house sells?
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 stays on the tax bill for the whole fiscal year that follows. Waltham's Assessors explain that value and ownership are fixed as of January 1, so a buyer who closes later in the year receives bills addressed to the previous owner, in care of the new owner.

The buyer's own name appears as assessed owner starting with the next fiscal year. The Collector asks new owners to notify the Assessors Office, and the Assessors cannot change the name until a new deed arrives from the Registry of Deeds. They will add the new owner to the mailing address in the meantime so the bills reach the right person.

State law adds one protection. Under M.G.L. c. 59, section 59, a person who gets title after January 1 is treated as a taxpayer for abatement purposes, so a buyer can still ask for an abatement on a bill that carries the seller's name.

sections.h2: What is the Waltham residential exemption, and who can use it?
sections.html:
The residential exemption lowers the assessed value of an owner-occupied home, and for fiscal year 2026 Waltham set it at $317,643. It applies to a principal residence of up to three units.

The city lists these requirements as of January 1:

  • You own the home.
  • It is your principal residence, the same one you use for income tax purposes.
  • If the home is held in a trust, you file a copy of the trust with the Assessors for review.

For fiscal year 2026 the owner had to have occupied the home and been the owner of record on January 1, 2025. Owners who are not already receiving it have until April 1 each year to apply. The exemption shows up on the third quarter actual bill, and an approved late application is credited to the fourth quarter bill or refunded if the tax is already paid in full.

A property that is not anyone's principal residence does not qualify, so a buyer who rents the house out may pay more than the seller did.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Waltham assessment?
sections.html:
You challenge a Waltham assessment by filing an abatement application with the Assessors Office, and the state deadline is tied to the first actual tax bill. M.G.L. c. 59, section 59 says the application is due on or before the last day to pay the first installment of the actual bill without interest. In Waltham the third quarter bill is the first actual bill and it is due February 1, so plan around that date and confirm the exact deadline with the Assessors.

The city posts a state Form 128 for abatements. Waltham's assessors say they value a home the way a buyer would, looking at location, interior condition, size, and kitchen and bath quality, then comparing sales in the neighborhood and adjusting for differences. They ask applicants to be specific about the reason for the complaint.

Useful evidence includes:

  • Errors on the property record card, such as the wrong square footage or bathroom count.
  • Recent sales of comparable homes that sold for less than your assessment.
  • Photos or repair estimates showing a condition that the assessment did not reflect.

A tenant who pays more than half the taxes under a lease may also apply, and mail counts as filed on its United States postmark date.

sections.h2: Does Waltham offer tax relief for older or disabled owners?
sections.html:
Yes, Waltham runs a Tax Relief Program through its Taxation Fund Committee for low-income elderly and low-income disabled residents. The fund pays part of the real estate tax for people who meet its guidelines, and preference goes to the applicants with the greatest need.

Applications are available from July 1 through November 5 at the Assessors Office, City Hall, 25 Lexington Street, 781-314-3200. The fund is supported by donations that residents can check off on the envelope enclosed with the tax bill. The Treasurer/Collector also lists a Senior Work Off Program among its services.

sections.h2: What shapes the Waltham housing market?
sections.html:
Waltham's housing market is shaped by its jobs base, its colleges and its rail and highway links. The city lists Bentley University, Brandeis University, Fresenius Medical Care North America, National Grid, Constant Contact and Vistaprint among its largest non-city employers in the 2023 annual financial report, each in the 1,000 to 4,999 employee range.

TopicFact
NicknameWatch City, from the Waltham Watch Company factory that opened in 1854
First of its kindBoston Manufacturing Company, the first integrated textile mill in the United States
HighwaysInterstate 95 runs with Route 128 through the western part; Interstate 90 is just south in Newton
Commuter railTwo MBTA Fitchburg Line stops, one at Central Square across from City Hall and one near Brandeis
BusMBTA routes 61, 70, 170, 505, 553, 554, 556 and 558
Public schoolsSeven elementary schools, McDevitt and Kennedy middle schools, and Waltham High School

Companies with a large presence include Revvity, RTX's Raytheon business, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Alkermes and Boston Dynamics. Retail clusters along Main Street, Moody Street, Lexington Street, River Street and parts of Route 60.

Neighborhood names include Piety Corner, Banks Square, Warrendale, the Bleachery, the Highlands and the North Side. The Charles River runs through the city.

sections.h2: What should a seller do about Waltham property tax before closing?
sections.html:
A seller should ask the Treasurer/Collector for a current balance and for a municipal lien certificate, since that office issues them and also runs the tax title program. A lien certificate lists what is owed against the property.

We did not find the fee or turnaround time for a Waltham lien certificate on a page we could open, so call 781-314-3250 and ask before you set a closing date. We also could not confirm the current Waltham tax rate on an official page, so check your latest bill or ask the Assessors rather than relying on a number found elsewhere.

A short checklist for owners with taxes due:

  • Pull your last four quarterly bills and note which are paid.
  • Ask the Collector whether interest at 14 percent a year has been added.
  • Tell the Assessors if you recently bought, so future bills carry your name.

faqs.q: When are Waltham property taxes due?
faqs.a: Waltham bills are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. If a date falls on a weekend, payment is due the next business day, according to the Treasurer/Collector.

faqs.q: How much interest does Waltham charge on late real estate tax?
faqs.a: The Treasurer/Collector says unpaid bills are subject to interest of 14 percent a year. Call 781-314-3250 for the exact amount on your account.

faqs.q: Can I get a Waltham tax abatement if I just bought the house?
faqs.a: Yes. M.G.L. c. 59, section 59 treats a person who acquires title after January 1 as a taxpayer for abatement purposes. File with the Assessors Office and confirm the deadline with them.

faqs.q: Why does my Waltham bill still show the old owner?
faqs.a: Ownership is set as of January 1 for the whole fiscal year. A buyer who closes after that date gets bills addressed in care of the new owner, and the buyer's name appears the following fiscal year.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Waltham tax lien certificate?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer/Collector at 781-314-3250. Ask for the fee, how long it takes and whether the office needs the request in writing.
